- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to match sentiment-driven momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overcorrects downward — adjust forecast to allow for mean reversion but not excessive pullback.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price peaks in early 30-day horizon — apply a +2 to +5% upward bias for peak days.  
- Model overestimates late-period prices (last 5–7 days of 30d) — apply downward bias of 1–3% for final 7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term volatility (e.g., alternating +/–), model fails to capture momentum — use moving average of last 5 sentiment values to adjust forecast slope.
